task: t7 (B1) — resolve the session workspace root in every mpd plugin via one adapter helper
decision_record: t1 (Architect) — implemented as written: adapter.workspaceRoot(exec) with precedence session header cwd -> DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT -> process.cwd(), plus adapter.workspaceRootsAll() (union of live session cwds, [] when the registry is absent). No disagreement with the record.
defect: Every self-written mpd plugin resolved state with `process.env.DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT ?? process.cwd()`, but the installed harness never defines DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT (measured 0 occurrences), so the expression collapsed to the dsh process cwd (/root/dshProj) while the session workspace is /root/dshProj/my-power-dsh. Boulder/memory/verif/hashline/ulw/config/comment-checker/modelchain state and the workmate in-use gate all pointed at the wrong (shared) directory.

fix.one_resolution: packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/src/index.ts — module-level `workspaceRootOf(exec)` (session -> env -> cwd) and `workspaceRootsOf(agents)`; the row instance exposes them as `dsh.workspaceRoot(exec)` / `dsh.workspaceRootsAll()`. No plugin reads exec.agent/session or ctx.agents itself.
call_sites: mpd-boulder: boulderRoot(config, dsh, exec) — every tool body resolves PER CALL
mpd-hashline: registry file + every relative tool path resolve against the session workspace (mirrors dsh-tool-bash workdir resolution)
mpd-memory: slug + store root per call (slug now follows the session workspace basename)
mpd-ulw: planDir/stateDir moved OUT of the apply-time consts into the tool body
mpd-modelchain: memory.json path resolved in both tool bodies
mpd-config: apply-time snapshot keeps the exec-less form (documented), BOTH tools re-read with the session root
mpd-comment-checker: hookInputFor cwd = session workspace (fallback via workspaceRootOf)

mpd-verif: env.workspaceRoot(exec)/venvPath(override, exec)/workDir(exec)/paths(venv, exec) forwarded through compile/coverage/regress/sim/uvm/venv and all 8 tool bodies; the duplicate sim.wsResolved() was deleted

mpd-workmate: busyTeams(key, roots) scans the given workspace roots; tool path = [session root], service/route path = agentlessRoots(dsh) = union of live session roots falling back to the env/cwd form
fix.explicit_overrides_preserved: boulder.dir, hashline.registryFile, memory.dir/agentSlug, ulw.planDir/stateDir, config.projectFile, MPD_DSH_VERIF_VENV/WORK, commentChecker paths — all still win over the root (precedence step 0).

findings.problem: packages/mpd-codegraph-plugin/src/index.ts:76 still resolves `(MPD_CODEGRAPH_PROJECT_CWD ?? MPD_DSH_CODEGRAPH_PROJECT_CWD) || process.cwd()` at APPLY time. t1 §2 A14/§4 deliberately keeps it apply-time (a boot side effect), but the record also notes it could route through dsh.workspaceRoot() with no exec so there is one code path.
findings.requiredFix: Out of t7's inScope (mpd-codegraph-plugin is not listed). Follow-up: swap the expression for dsh.workspaceRoot() (exec-less) and optionally resolve the `/mpd-codegraph` command per invocation (F6 of the record shows invocation.agent exists).

findings.problem: mpd-config's APPLY-TIME snapshot stays process-scoped (t1 L1): it mounts before its consumers, which merge config at apply. A project layer living in a session workspace different from the process root is therefore invisible to the apply-time snapshot (the two TOOLS are session-aware now).
findings.requiredFix: Recorded, not fixed: a per-session config service is a follow-up (would change the mpdConfig service API, explicitly out of t7 scope).

findings.problem: MCP children (mpd-mcp-astgrep/lsp/codegraph dists) are separate processes with no exec and keep the launch-cwd fallback (t1 L2/E).
findings.requiredFix: None in t7 — they accept explicit cwd/workdir arguments; a session-scoped default would need a wired env channel.

findings.problem: The memory store is SPLIT-BRAIN (t1 §5 M1): 7 commits live in the wrong-root store /root/dshProj/.mpd/memory/agents/agent-dshproj, while the correct-root store <repo>/.mpd/memory/agents/agent-my-power-dsh already exists (20 files, 19 steps). After this fix the plugins read the CORRECT root, so those 7 wrong-root entries are now orphaned.
findings.requiredFix: Deliberately NOT performed here: .mpd/** is not a declared path of t7 and the store is live, git-backed user data; migrating it is a data decision for the captain/user (t1 M1 describes the exact merge, including keeping the correct-root reflection counter). Until then the orphan store stays untouched at /root/dshProj/.mpd (t1 M2: do not delete it).

findings.problem: OUT-OF-SCOPE BUT REQUIRED EDIT: skills/dsh-qa/scripts/workmate-library.mjs pins three exact source literals of the mutation surface. The B1 fix extends that API (teamRoots/roots parameter), so the three pins were updated to the new literals (route paths, POST-only rule and the §D reason matrix are unchanged). Declared here for captain ratification because skills/** is not in t7's inScope list.
findings.requiredFix: Ratify the edit (or, if the captain prefers, revert the API extension and carry the roots through another channel — the QA gate `bun run test:qa` is a REQUIRED verify command of this task and cannot pass otherwise).

findings.problem: The mpdWorkmate service `rename`/`delete` gained an optional trailing `roots?: string[]`; the mpd_workmate_* TOOL schemas are unchanged (they still accept the same arguments).
findings.requiredFix: None — no in-repo consumer of the service exists (the Web client uses the HTTP routes); the routes and their reason codes are unchanged.

findings.problem: Behaviour change worth naming: mpd_hashline_read/edit/format/restore now resolve RELATIVE paths against the session workspace (previously the process cwd). Absolute paths are unchanged, and the registry file moved to <session workspace>/.mpd/hashline-files.json.
findings.requiredFix: None — this is the defect; it mirrors the harness bash tool's workdir resolution (t1 F5). Callers that relied on the process cwd for relative paths were relying on the bug.

notes: The proof is one boot with THREE live sessions (repo, W_BLOCKED, W_CLEAN) in ONE process: it proves the resolution is per-session (multi-session host) and not a process-wide redirect.
